newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S.Korea gas oil exports seen rising on expansion.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea gas oil exports seen rising on expansion.

text.p: South Korea's gas oil exports are expected to rise to nearly 4.5 million barrels a month by the end of this year following a flurry of capacity expansions, traders in Seoul said on Thursday.

Yukong Ltd, the nation's largest oil refiner, plans to raise its monthly gas oil exports to 1.5 million barrels with full operation of its new 200,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU), a company source told Reuters.
The unit's commercial production is expected by September 30, he said.

Yukong currently exports an average of 1.0-1.2 million barrels of gas oil a month, he said. oil major Caltex Petroleum Corp, sees itself turning to gas oil exports from imports when its new 220,000-bpd CDU comes on stream. It is expected to start test running the unit in October.
"It's hard to estimate the size of the exports, but we'll start to export gas oil when the new unit begins production," said a trader at LG-Caltex.
He did not indicate how much volumes will be exported but trading sources expect LG-Caltex to export about 400,000 barrels a month.
LG-Caltex, formerly known as Honam Oil Refining Co, has been concentrating on meeting local demand for gas oil, traders said. Caltex is a joint-venture between Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc.
Despite the expansions by Yukong and LG-Caltex, Ssangyong Oil Refining Co will remain South Korea's largest exporter of gas oil, traders said.

Ssangyong's gas oil exports stands at 1.76 million barrels a month, traders said. South Korea's other refiners, Hyundai Oil Refinery Co and Hanwha Energy Co, exports 400,000 barrels of gas oil per month each.

Traders in Singapore said that they have already started seeing more gas oil cargoes being offered by Korean refiners. For example, in September Korean refiners offered between seven and 10 gas oil cargoes of 25,000-30,000 tonnes each.
Most of the cargoes were heard to have been sold to China and Korean traders said that only one September cargo was still left.
Traders said China will be the main target for Korean gas oil supplies as its geographical proximity allows for savings on freight costs.
